chapter: Funerals, second lines and being an outsider
title: Waiting outside funerals; never following to the cemetery
summary: Wood fraternized with musicians over beer while services ran, and never followed a funeral into the cemetery.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: And I used to, uh, when they were going to funerals, uh, when the procession would get in the church and they would have that part of it, the preaching and the singing of the choir. Yeah. The band would frequently just be sitting around outside waiting for them to come out. Mm-hmm. And, uh, you know, would sit on a curb and buy a beer at the grocery store on the block down the street and sit and drink a beer with them and talk to the musicians. Uh, or maybe go up and sit on the ground under the church window and try to listen to the choir singing inside. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm.
But they could stay in there a long time preaching over the deceased an hour sometime.
So you had a little time to kill, and it was a hot sunset. So you found a bit of shade, buy a beer, and fraternize with your musicians. On a very casual level. Yeah, oh, yeah.
Not going into the church. Oh, no. You never had to make a statement or testify to the congregation? No. Or going to any of the dinners or anything like that?
Always sort of hanging around in the background.
Yeah, well, you didn't want to intrude.
And actually, that feeling of not wanting to intrude, I never went, I never followed a funeral all the way into the cemetery.
I never went and saw them actually bury the deceased and, you know, just hung around and gawked at that part of it.
Well, it was nobody you knew.
I mean, maybe a musician who died.

Well, I might have done that, but I wasn't here when the musician died. And, yeah, that would have been a different situation. But anyway, it was just a total stranger. I didn't think it. My sensibilities were such that I cut myself off at that point and I wouldn't follow them into the cemetery.
